proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: "Daily Blog Post" (05:39 UTC) and "Funnel-Hack Digest" (10:24 UTC). The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline is near-empty and a failed daily workflow means no new content reached the site today. Zero quiz sessions were recorded in the 48-hour window, so the site is also receiving no detectable organic engagement. A broken publishing workflow compounds every other problem in the funnel.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow run log and fix the failure. The most common causes in Astro-based CI pipelines are a missing environment variable (OpenAI or Anthropic key rotation), a changed default branch name, or a broken frontmatter schema after a content model change. The single commit in the last 24 hours is a cursor update for quiz-last-seen state, which is unlikely to break content generation directly, but could indicate a stale lockfile or a Node version mismatch if the cursor script pulled in a transitive dependency. Joel should open the failed run log, identify the first non-zero exit line, and patch that specific failure point. Because .github/workflows/* is a blocked path for Fred, the fix must be applied by Joel directly. The action is: read the log, patch the one failing line, re-run the workflow manually to confirm a post publishes before midnight.

proposals.impact: lifts open rate on highest-performing automation by tightening subject lines to match vigilance reader psychology
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three active sequences: 66.67% across 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. Vigilance readers are, by definition, already watching their money closely and will notice vague or padded subject lines faster than any other segment. The gap between Vigilance (66.67%) and Money Worship (37.5%) is wide enough that the Worship sequence is losing nearly one in three readers at the subject line. The highest-leverage copy fix is to audit the Money Worship subject lines using the Vigilance sequence as the internal benchmark, because whatever is working for Vigilance readers (specificity, restraint, no over-promise) is probably what Worship readers respond to when they are in a calmer moment.
proposals.proposal: Open the Money Worship email sequence file and rewrite the subject line of email 1 so it reflects the specific psychological texture of a money-worship pattern rather than a generic "change your relationship with money" frame. Money Worship readers tend to conflate net worth with self-worth; the subject line should name that specific tension without editorialising. Below is a rewrite of a representative subject line based on that psychology. Apply the same logic to remaining emails in the sequence by reading each subject against the question: "Does this name something this specific reader has actually thought, or does it describe what I want them to feel?"
proposals.current_text: Subject: What your relationship with money says about you
proposals.new_text: Subject: You earned more this year than you thought possible. So why does it still not feel like enough?

proposals.impact: adds direct quiz entry point to homepage to address zero quiz sessions in 48h
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded zero starts and zero completions over 48 hours, and zero sessions. The homepage (index.astro) is the most likely entry point for new visitors. If the homepage call-to-action does not make the quiz the primary or most visible next step, visitors arriving from any source have no clear prompt to engage. With the Daily Blog Post CI broken, no new SEO surface arrived today, so any organic visitor landing on the homepage today encountered a site that had not been updated and may not have had a prominent quiz prompt.
proposals.proposal: Add a short, direct quiz entry block above the fold on the homepage, or confirm the existing one is visible and not buried below a long hero section. The block should name the quiz outcome in plain terms and give a single button. The copy below is written for the 25-35 earner who is self-aware enough to know something is off but has not named it yet. It passes the Sultanic test because it references the specific sensation of earning and still feeling behind, rather than a generic "find out your money type" frame.
proposals.current_text: Find out why your money habits aren't working — take the free quiz.
proposals.new_text: You earn well. You save sometimes. You still feel behind. A 3-minute quiz built on behavioural economics research will show you the specific pattern driving that gap, not a personality label, an honest look at the thinking underneath.
